DvaitaVedanta._visibility_note: Not linked in the Library nav for a normal reader, excluded from global search results, and not rendered without an admin unlock. SetuTila._readme: Setu Tila edition of the Sarvamula (setutila.in), imported by tools/setutila/import_setutila.py with block UUIDs + pathantara variant readings preserved; works registered hidden in library.json pending review.

shankara_bhashya._note: Adi Shankaracharya's Prasthanatrayi bhashya -- Brahmasutra, ten Upanishads, and the Gita. Mirrors how sarvamoola_grantha holds Madhva's corpus above. Default keeps each work whole in a single bhashya leaf (no separate mula split yet) -- see importers/shankara_bhashya.py for why.

yamunacharya._note: Yamunacharya (Alavandar), Ramanuja's predecessor's guru's guru -- Samvitsiddhi is part of his Siddhitrayam, a refutation of Advaitic positions on consciousness/self. Moved here 25 Aug 2026 from agama.pratyabhijna, where it had been misfiled by title-word ("samvit") rather than by author/tradition -- GRETIL identifies it plainly as Yamunacarya's work, and its own opening line states the Advaita purva-paksha it goes on to refute.

vishnu_smriti._default_author: Maharshi Vishnu (smriti-rishi, distinct from the deity)

smriti._note: Apastamba and Gautama Dharmasutras were empty duplicate leaves here -- the real, populated texts (853 and 891 items) already live correctly classified under vedanga.kalpa.krishna_yajurveda.apastamba.dharmasutra and vedanga.kalpa.independent_dharmasutras.gautama_dharmasutra, found and confirmed via DCS (github.com/OliverHellwig/sanskrit) 25 Aug 2026. Removed rather than duplicated -- Apastamba/Gautama are properly Kalpa-sutra school texts, not independent verse Smritis.

agama._note: Restructured 25 Aug 2026 -- was flattening sectarian traditions (Pancharatra/Pashupata/Pratyabhijna/Shaiva Siddhanta/Natha), scriptural corpora (Shakta Agama) and philosophical schools as if they were parallel top-level categories. See dge/PENDING.md for the individual reclassifications and the sourcing behind each one -- Samvitsiddhi moved out entirely to darshana.vedanta.vishishtadvaita.yamunacharya (it's Yamunacharya's Vedantic refutation of Advaita, not a Kashmir Saiva philosophical text).

pancharatra._default_author: Traditionally revealed (Divya Prabandha of Bhagavan Narayana); human compiler varies by samhita and is often unrecorded

pancharatra_samhitas._note: Regrouped 25 Aug 2026 per the traditional Ratnatraya/Pramukha distinction (Sattvata/Paushkara/Jayakhya as the three Divya 'jewel' samhitas) rather than one flat list of 15 siblings. Guna (Sattvika/Rajasa/Tamasa) and Madhva-relevance are kept as per-text metadata fields, not folders -- see each samhita's data.json and dge/PENDING.md.

tika._default_author: Narayanakantha (DCS metadata unconfirmed -- inferred from the text's standard scholarly name)

bhashya_kaundinya._default_author: Kaundinya (DCS metadata unconfirmed -- inferred from the text's standard scholarly name)

shaiva_tantra._note: Non-dual/Bhairava-adjacent Shaiva tantric works whose GRETIL corpus placement is Shaiva despite strong Goddess/Mahavidya content in some of them (deity orientation is not the same axis as sectarian corpus classification).

uddamareshvara_tantra._note: Predominantly prayoga/ritual material (vasikarana, uccatana, stambhana, mohana, medicinal procedures) per older manuscript cataloguing, not a primarily liberation-oriented scripture.

shakta_shaiva._note: Works genuinely straddling Shakta and Shaiva material (deity, ritual, and alchemical content mixed) -- kept as their own bucket rather than forced into either parent.

kashmir_shaivism._note: Split out 25 Aug 2026 from the too-narrow 'Pratyabhijna' node, which had wrongly been made the parent of Trika/Spanda/Shiva-Sutra material as if they were all one school.

shakta_vijnana._note: By Somananda; the text calls its own teaching sakta-vijnana and places itself within Trika sastra -- title-word alone would misfile this as generic Shakta.

vatulanatha_sutras._note: Kashmir Saiva Krama/Yogini transmission -- 'natha' here is the honorific, not the Gorakhnath Natha lineage.

shiva_sutra._note: Vasugupta's root text and Bhaskara's Vartika kept together -- previously the root sat under a generic top-level 'shaiva_agama' leaf while its own commentary sat under a different 'pratyabhijna' branch.

natha_hathayoga._note: Split 25 Aug 2026: Gheranda Samhita and Hathayogapradipika are classical Hathayoga-corpus manuals (real Natha connections, but 'Hathayoga text' is the more useful primary classification); Amaraughashasana and Gorakshashataka are the actual Natha/Gorakshanatha scriptural corpus.

stotra._readme: Flat by design -- see ARCHITECTURE_DECISIONS.md 'Folders vs tags'. Deity/theme grouping is done via the 'deity' field in each stotra's own metadata and surfaced in the Library UI, not via folder nesting. This keeps published paths stable forever and avoids ever duplicating a text across two locations.

shabdapatha._note: Not shloka-shaped, same as dhatupatha above -- opens dge/shabda.html directly (see DGE_SPECIAL_PAGES in js/library.js), never the general reader. Added to the library tree 20 Aug -- it existed as real, populated data (9007 words) and its own page, but had no taxonomy/library.json entry at all, so it was unreachable by browsing the library, only by a direct URL or the Explore popup.

dasa_sahitya._note: Haridasa devotional compositions (padas/suladis/ugabhogas/...) from four independently-sourced collections (web crawl, Android app, Firestore export, flat-JSON dump), reviewed and merged into one corpus 21 Aug 2026 -- see dge/data/dasa_sahitya_local/ARCHITECTURE.md for the full review history. Registered here as real leaves under 'composers' (25 Aug 2026); dasa_sahitya.html still reads the same files directly via data/dasa_sahitya/index.json for its own bespoke browsing UI. 'dasakuta' above kept only Jagannathadasa's Harikathamritasara -- a distinct kavya, not a pada -- after its empty per-composer pada/suladi/ugabhoga stub (superseded by 'composers') was removed. 'vyasakuta' (Sanskrit prakaranas by Madhva-tradition acharyas) is a separate, unrelated corpus.

upaveda._note: Traditional Upaveda (subsidiary Veda) subjects, distinct from the four Vedas proper and from vedanga. Placement decision made 20 Aug 2026 (was an open question in PENDING.md) put Ayurveda and Kamashastra here as their traditional classification. Reversed 28 Aug 2026, project lead's explicit correction: Kamashastra is not traditionally one of the Upavedas in most classical enumerations (the common list is Ayurveda/Dhanurveda/Gandharvaveda/Arthashastra or Sthapatyaveda) -- moved out entirely to shastra.kama_shastra, consolidating it with the independently-added shastra/kama_shastra/mula duplicate found there at the same time (see core.js DGE_LEGACY_SLUGS). Ayurveda stays here. This same 28 Aug pass also merged in a second, uncoordinated 'vedas.upaveda' tree (fuller Ayurveda Samhita/Rasashastra content plus a real Dhanurveda text) that had grown up nested under vedas/ instead of here, and added Gandharvaveda/Sthapatyaveda as honest pending placeholders to round out the traditional four -- Nitishastra is kept as its own separate top-level section below since it is not traditionally an Upaveda either.

misc._note: Holding place for material whose home in the taxonomy is not settled yet. Nothing is meant to stay here; each item moves once it is decided.
